Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)

Required findings: Greater than six (6) months since the prior cervical decompression or cervical fusion at an adjacent level

Symptoms include BOTH significant level of pain on a daily basis defined as clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing) AND unremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability

Physical exam findings include ANY of: dermatomal sensory deficit, motor deficit (e.g., biceps, triceps weakness), reflex changes, shoulder abduction relief sign, nerve root tension sign (e.g., Spurling's maneuver), or unremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity without concordant objective physical exam findings

Less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated): prescription strength analgesics/steroids/gabapentinoids/NSAIDs for six (6) weeks, provider-directed exercise program for six (6) weeks, or epidural steroid injection(s)/selective nerve root block(s) at the same level(s) as requested surgery

Plain x-rays of the cervical spine (including flexion/extension lateral views) and advanced diagnostic imaging show successful decompression and fusion at the previous operative level; MRI/CT shows neural structure compression at the requested level(s) concordant with symptoms/exam caused by herniated disc(s), synovial/arachnoid cyst, central/lateral/foraminal stenosis, or osteophytes

Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders) AND documentation of nicotine-free status (never-smoker OR refrained from smoking/tobacco/nicotine replacement for at least six (6) weeks prior to surgery validated by objective cotinine testing within normal range)
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-601.7: Adjacent Segment Disease > Radiculopathy (TOC: S12.1.1)

Required findings: Symptoms include ANY of: upper/lower extremity weakness, numbness, or pain; fine motor dysfunction (buttoning, handwriting, clumsiness of hands); gait disturbance; new-onset bowel or bladder dysfunction; or frequent falls

Physical exam findings include ANY of: grip and release test, ataxic gait, hyperreflexia, Hoffmann sign, Babinski sign, tandem walking test demonstrating ataxia, inverted brachial radial reflex, increased muscle tone or spasticity, clonus, or myelopathic hand
MRI/CT shows findings concordant with symptoms and physical exam findings caused by EITHER cervical spinal cord compression OR cervical spinal stenosis
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-601.7: Adjacent Segment Disease > Myelopathy (TOC: S12.1.2)

Non-Indications: ACDF for adjacent segment disease performed less than six (6) months after the prior cervical decompression or fusion

Radiculopathy cases where the patient has not demonstrated less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least two of the required conservative management modalities (medications, exercise, injections) for the specified duration, unless contraindicated
Cases where imaging does not show successful decompression and fusion at the previous operative level
Cases where MRI/CT findings of neural compression are not concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings
Presence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders)
Failure to document nicotine-free status via never-smoker history or objective cotinine testing (serum, urinary, or saliva) within normal range for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery
Important criteria & exceptions: Conservative management requirements for radiculopathy apply unless contraindicated
Nicotine-free status can be validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the specific testing method and lab

For radiculopathy, physical exam findings may include 'unremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity without concordant objective physical exam findings' as a qualifying criterion alongside other objective signs
Documentation required: Plain x-rays of the cervical spine including flexion/extension lateral views
Advanced diagnostic imaging (MRI/CT) reports showing successful decompression and fusion at the previous operative level and neural structure compression at the requested level(s)

Records of conservative management including prescription medication logs (analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, NSAIDs) for six weeks, provider-directed exercise program records for six weeks, and/or records of epidural steroid injections or selective nerve root blocks
Objective cotinine testing results (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within normal range, or documentation of never-smoker status
Documentation of mental and behavioral health status confirming absence of unmanaged significant disorders
